verdict.line: You lose if you poke Q-for-Q into his longer-ranged Parrrley or all-in while Remove Scurvy is up; you win if you save Shadow Dash for the moment his W is down and use Stand United to make your presence felt elsewhere on the map.

brief.thesis: Gangplank's Parrrley (625 range) outranges your Vorpal Blade (475 range), so he poke-farms you for free while you have no answer except absorbing it. His W, Remove Scurvy, clears your only hard CC and heals him back, so Shadow Dash all-ins only work on a timer. Your real edge isn't the 1v1 — it's that Stand United lets you abandon a losing lane state and swing fights elsewhere, which is why Shen holds a 51.4% win rate overall even though this specific matchup sits at 48.7% across 1,773 games.

theirWindow.what: He can poke you freely with Parrrley and simply cleanse-and-heal through anything you land, so don't commit Shadow Dash or a full trade here — you'll just hand him a free Remove Scurvy heal.

yourWindow.when: Right after he burns Remove Scurvy
yourWindow.what: This is your real all-in window — dash in with Shadow Dash to taunt him, land Vorpal Blade, and lean on Ignite or your boots' armor to close the trade before W (22/21/20/19/18s) comes back up.

start.why: Its passive block and regen are the direct answer to a melee laner who out-ranges you and wants to chip you down with Parrrley before you can even reach him; 84% of Shen players into this matchup start it for a reason.

boots.why: Flat basic-attack damage reduction blunts both his auto-attack trades and the per-second poison from Grog-Soaked Blade, which stacks every time his autos land.

core.why: Gives you the wave-clear and health/AD scaling to keep pace in farm and close distance for a trade, since you can't out-poke his ranged Q.
The flat stat spike keeps your effective HP high enough that his stacking Grog-Soaked Blade poison doesn't quietly win the attrition war.
The active slow directly punishes a champion who lives off landing autos to stack poison and land killing Parrrleys for gold.

situational.when: he's stacking on-hit or crit damage and you need grievous wounds to cut his Remove Scurvy heal and poison sustain
you need an earlier, cheaper piece of armor and anti-heal before your Randuin's or Thornmail finishes
the game runs long and you want a scaling health item for sustained teamfight tankiness
your team needs more peel and utility than raw damage mitigation in the later game

runes.keystoneWhy: Procs off minions in melee range and heals/damages passively, offsetting the chip damage you take simply standing in range of his ranged Parrrley poke.

summoners.why: Ignite punishes the short window right after his Remove Scurvy heal is spent, denying the sustain he just paid a cooldown for; Flash+Teleport is the close second pick (33.2%) if you'd rather prioritize sidelane pressure with your ultimate instead of forcing kills.

playing.title: Follow the Q-E-W skill order
playing.detail: The highest win-rate order takes Q at 1, E at 2, W at 3, then maxes Q before finishing E and W, grabbing R at 6/11/16. Prioritize Q for wave state and trades — Feint's cooldown only matters once you're actually locked into a fight.

playing.title: Don't trade Q for Q
playing.detail: Vorpal Blade's 475 range loses the poke war to his 625-range Parrrley every time. Hold your Q for when you're already on top of him, not as an answer to his harass.

playing.title: Angle Shadow Dash through the wave
playing.detail: Shadow Dash taunts every enemy champion it passes through on its way to the target location, so route it through the minion wave rather than straight at him — it stops him from sidestepping behind creeps to dodge the taunt.

playing.title: Time your all-in around Remove Scurvy
playing.detail: Committing Shadow Dash while his W is up just gives him a free cleanse-and-heal. Wait until he's spent it on poison or CC from elsewhere before you commit.

playing.title: Use Stand United to swing side lanes
playing.detail: Since you're a slight underdog in the straight 1v1, Stand United's teleport lets you abandon a stalemated wave and show up for a sidelane skirmish or objective instead of forcing an even trade you don't need.

playing.title: Don't facetank through Grog-Soaked Blade
playing.detail: Feint absorbs incoming damage only for a few seconds; standing in extended autos lets his stacking poison keep ticking after the shield expires, so end trades before Feint runs out, not after.

brief.patchCaveat: Win rates, build paths, runes, and summoner spells here are pulled directly from measured OP.GG games on patch 16.19.1; the timing windows, dash angling, and trade-pattern advice are my own tactical reading of the ability kits, not measured data.

stats.opponentTip: Use Doran’s Shield and [P] to shield the damage on Gangplank’s (Q). Gangplank’s (W) can free him of Taunt, making it difficult to fight him. Engage aggressively when (W) is on cooldown.
